card.title: Drones for Deliveries
card.passage: Today, some companies are testing drones to deliver goods. Drones can fly over roads and rivers, and in this way they can reach places that are hard to get to by car. Companies hope that drones will help people living in mountain areas. However, drones can be affected by bad weather, so companies need to make sure they can fly safely.

bubbles.t: Let's go to Okinawa this summer!

panels.cap: On the day of the trip

card.start: One day, Mr. and Mrs. Sato were talking about their summer vacation.

steps.t: First, please read the passage silently for 20 seconds.
All right. Now, please read it aloud.
Now, I'll ask you four questions.
Number 1. According to the passage, how can drones reach places that are hard to get to by car?
Number 2. Now, please look at the pictures and describe the situation. You have 20 seconds to prepare. Your story should begin with the sentence on the card.
Please begin.
Now, please turn over the card and put it down.
Number 3. Some people say that families should spend more time together. What do you think about that?

points: and in this way / However, の前で区切る
内容のまとまりを意識して

q1.q: According to the passage, how can drones reach places that are hard to get to by car?
q1.ja: ドローンはどうやって車で行きにくい場所に届くことができますか。
model: By flying over roads and rivers.
points: in this way の前を答える

q2.ja: 3コマのイラストの話を、カードの最初の文から説明してください。
model: One day, Mr. and Mrs. Sato were talking about their summer vacation. Mrs. Sato said to her husband, "Let's go to Okinawa this summer!" A week later, Mr. Sato was booking plane tickets on his computer, and Mrs. Sato was packing a suitcase. On the day of the trip, they were at the airport. They found out that their flight had been canceled because of a typhoon.
points: 2人がそれぞれしていることを説明
過去完了(had been canceled)も使えると◎

q3.q: Some people say that families should spend more time together. What do you think about that?
q3.ja: 家族はもっと一緒に過ごすべきだという意見について、どう思いますか。
model: I agree. Spending time together helps family members understand each other. For example, they can talk about their problems during dinner.
I disagree. Many people are busy with work and school. It is more important for families to enjoy the time they have together.
points: I agree / I disagree で立場を

card.title: Face Recognition at Airports
card.passage: Today, some airports are using face recognition technology. Passengers have their faces scanned instead of showing their passports and tickets many times. Airports can check passengers more quickly, and by doing so they can make waiting times shorter. However, some people worry about how their personal information is used, so airports need to explain how they protect it.

bubbles.t: I want to watch the airplanes from the observation deck!

card.start: One day, Mrs. Ito and her son were at the airport.

steps.t: First, please read the passage silently for 20 seconds.
All right. Now, please read it aloud.
Now, I'll ask you four questions.
Number 1. According to the passage, how can airports make waiting times shorter?
Number 2. Now, please look at the pictures and describe the situation. You have 20 seconds to prepare. Your story should begin with the sentence on the card.
Please begin.
Now, please turn over the card and put it down.
Number 3. Some people say that technology is making people's lives less private. What do you think about that?

points: face recognition technology をひとまとまりで
by doing so の前で区切る

q1.q: According to the passage, how can airports make waiting times shorter?
q1.ja: 空港はどうやって待ち時間を短くできますか。
model: By checking passengers more quickly.
points: by doing so の前を答える

q2.ja: 3コマのイラストの話を、カードの最初の文から説明してください。
model: One day, Mrs. Ito and her son were at the airport. Her son said to her, "I want to watch the airplanes from the observation deck!" An hour later, her son was watching airplanes through the window, and Mrs. Ito was buying souvenirs. A little later, they saw that it was the last call for their flight. They were running to the gate.
points: 2人がそれぞれしていることを説明
LAST CALL = 搭乗の最終案内

q3.q: Some people say that technology is making people's lives less private. What do you think about that?
q3.ja: テクノロジーによって生活のプライバシーが減っているという意見について、どう思いますか。
model: I agree. Many apps collect information about where we go and what we buy. Some companies use this information without asking us clearly.
I disagree. People can choose which information they share. Also, there are laws to protect personal information.
points: I agree / I disagree で立場を

card.title: Reducing Food Waste
card.passage: In Japan, a large amount of food is thrown away every day. Some restaurants give customers containers for food that they could not finish, and in this way they reduce food waste. Customers can enjoy the rest of their meals at home. However, food can go bad quickly in hot weather, so restaurants need to tell customers to eat it soon.

bubbles.t: Let's grow vegetables in our garden!

steps.t: First, please read the passage silently for 20 seconds.
All right. Now, please read it aloud.
Now, I'll ask you four questions.
Number 1. According to the passage, how do some restaurants reduce food waste?
Number 2. Now, please look at the pictures and describe the situation. You have 20 seconds to prepare. Your story should begin with the sentence on the card.
Please begin.
Now, please turn over the card and put it down.
Number 3. Some people say that people should buy only the food that they need. What do you think about that?

points: a large amount of をなめらかに
and in this way の前で区切る

q1.q: According to the passage, how do some restaurants reduce food waste?
q1.ja: いくつかのレストランはどうやって食品ロスを減らしていますか。
model: By giving customers containers for food that they could not finish.
points: in this way の前を答える

q2.ja: 3コマのイラストの話を、カードの最初の文から説明してください。
model: One day, Mr. and Mrs. Yamada were talking in the kitchen. Mrs. Yamada said to her husband, "Let's grow vegetables in our garden!" A few months later, Mr. Yamada was picking tomatoes, and Mrs. Yamada was carrying a basket. That evening, they had too many tomatoes. Mrs. Yamada was thinking of giving some of them to their neighbors.
points: 2人がそれぞれしていることを説明
3コマ目は考えていること(was thinking of ～ing)

q3.q: Some people say that people should buy only the food that they need. What do you think about that?
q3.ja: 必要な分だけ食べ物を買うべきだという意見について、どう思いますか。
model: I agree. If people buy too much food, they often throw some of it away. Planning meals before shopping can also save money.
I disagree. It is useful to keep some extra food at home. For example, people need food when a big disaster happens.
points: I agree / I disagree で立場を

card.title: Moving to the Countryside
card.passage: These days, the number of people living in the countryside is decreasing. Some towns offer cheap houses to young families from big cities. By doing so, they hope to bring more people to their towns. Young families can enjoy a quiet life surrounded by nature. However, there are not many jobs in some towns, so people need to think carefully before moving.

bubbles.t: Life in the countryside sounds nice.

card.start: One day, Mr. and Mrs. Ueda were at the station.

steps.t: First, please read the passage silently for 20 seconds.
All right. Now, please read it aloud.
Now, I'll ask you four questions.
Number 1. According to the passage, how do some towns hope to bring more people to their towns?
Number 2. Now, please look at the pictures and describe the situation. You have 20 seconds to prepare. Your story should begin with the sentence on the card.
Please begin.
Now, please turn over the card and put it down.
Number 3. Some people say that it is better for children to grow up in the countryside. What do you think about that?

points: By doing so, の文をはっきり

q1.q: According to the passage, how do some towns hope to bring more people to their towns?
q1.ja: いくつかの町はどうやって町に人を呼びたいと考えていますか。
model: By offering cheap houses to young families from big cities.
points: By doing so の前の文を答える

q2.ja: 3コマのイラストの話を、カードの最初の文から説明してください。
model: One day, Mr. and Mrs. Ueda were at the station. They saw a poster about living in Midori Town, and Mrs. Ueda said to her husband, "Life in the countryside sounds nice." A few months later, they were living in Midori Town. Mr. Ueda was growing vegetables, and Mrs. Ueda was walking their dog. One winter morning, there was a lot of snow, and Mr. Ueda couldn't use his car. He was worried that he would be late for work.
points: ポスターの内容も説明できると◎
3コマ目: 雪で車が使えない

q3.q: Some people say that it is better for children to grow up in the countryside. What do you think about that?
q3.ja: 子どもは田舎で育つほうがよいという意見について、どう思いますか。
model: I agree. Children can play outside in nature every day. They can also learn about farming and animals.
I disagree. In big cities, children can visit museums and choose from many different schools. They have more chances to learn new things.
points: I agree / I disagree で立場を

card.title: Disaster Information
card.passage: Japan has many natural disasters, such as earthquakes and heavy rain. Some local governments send emergency information to people's smartphones. People can quickly learn where they should go, and by doing so they can get to safe places in time. However, some elderly people do not use smartphones, so local governments also need other ways to give information.

bubbles.t: A big typhoon is coming this weekend.

card.start: One day, Saki was watching TV with her father.

steps.t: First, please read the passage silently for 20 seconds.
All right. Now, please read it aloud.
Now, I'll ask you four questions.
Number 1. According to the passage, how can people get to safe places in time?
Number 2. Now, please look at the pictures and describe the situation. You have 20 seconds to prepare. Your story should begin with the sentence on the card.
Please begin.
Now, please turn over the card and put it down.
Number 3. Some people say that schools should have more disaster drills. What do you think about that?

points: by doing so の前で区切る

q1.q: According to the passage, how can people get to safe places in time?
q1.ja: 人々はどうやって間に合うように安全な場所へ行くことができますか。
model: By quickly learning where they should go.
points: by doing so の前を答える

q2.ja: 3コマのイラストの話を、カードの最初の文から説明してください。
model: One day, Saki was watching TV with her father. Her father said to her, "A big typhoon is coming this weekend." The next day, they went shopping. Saki was holding a flashlight, and her father was putting water and canned food into the shopping cart. That night, there was a power outage because of the typhoon. Saki was using a flashlight, and her father was lighting a candle.
points: The next day / That night などコマの言葉を使う

q3.q: Some people say that schools should have more disaster drills. What do you think about that?
q3.ja: 学校は避難訓練をもっと行うべきだという意見について、どう思いますか。
model: I agree. Students need to know what to do when an earthquake happens. Practicing many times helps them move quickly and safely.
I disagree. Schools already have drills a few times a year. Students should spend more time on their classes.
points: I agree / I disagree で立場を

ek2_4.q: Today, many people buy things on the Internet. Do you think online shopping will become more popular in the future?
ek2_4.ja: 将来、ネットショッピングはもっと広まると思いますか。

model.yes: Yes. → It is convenient because people can buy things at any time. Also, delivery services are getting faster.
model.no: No. → Many people want to see products before they buy them. They also enjoy shopping with their friends at stores.

ek2_4.q: These days, many people pay without cash. Do you think cash will disappear in the future?
ek2_4.ja: 将来、現金はなくなると思いますか。

model.yes: Yes. → Paying by smartphone is fast and easy. Stores can also save time because they do not need to count money.
model.no: No. → Some elderly people are not used to cashless payments. Cash is also useful when there is a power outage.

ek2_4.q: Today, robots are used in many places. Do you think more robots will work in stores and restaurants in the future?
ek2_4.ja: 将来、店やレストランで働くロボットは増えると思いますか。

model.yes: Yes. → Many stores do not have enough workers. Robots can do simple jobs such as carrying food.
model.no: No. → Many customers want to talk with real people. Robots are also too expensive for small stores.

ek2_4.q: In Japan, the number of elderly people is increasing. Do you think the government should do more to help them?
ek2_4.ja: 政府は高齢者をもっと支援すべきだと思いますか。

model.yes: Yes. → Many elderly people live alone and need help in their daily lives. The government should build more care facilities.
model.no: No. → Families and local communities can support elderly people. The government also needs money for young people.

ek2_4.q: These days, many people get news from social media. Do you think the information on social media is reliable?
ek2_4.ja: SNSの情報は信頼できると思いますか。

model.yes: Yes. → People can get news quickly from people who are actually there. Many news companies also use social media.
model.no: No. → Anyone can post information on social media. Some of it is not true, so people need to be careful.

ek2_4.q: Today, many students take classes online. Do you think online classes are as good as classes at school?
ek2_4.ja: オンライン授業は学校の授業と同じくらい良いと思いますか。

model.yes: Yes. → Students can watch the lessons again and again. They can also study at their own pace.
model.no: No. → It is difficult to ask teachers questions online. Students also need to make friends at school.

ek2_4.q: Many foreign tourists visit Japan. Do you think there should be more signs in foreign languages?
ek2_4.ja: 外国語の案内表示をもっと増やすべきだと思いますか。

model.yes: Yes. → Tourists often get lost in big stations. Signs in many languages will help them travel safely.
model.no: No. → Many tourists can use translation apps on their smartphones. Too many signs can be confusing.

ek2_4.q: Some people say that companies should let workers take longer vacations. Do you think this is a good idea?
ek2_4.ja: 会社は社員にもっと長い休暇を取らせるべきだと思いますか。

model.yes: Yes. → Workers can relax and come back with more energy. They can also spend more time with their families.
model.no: No. → If many workers take long vacations, the company may not be able to do its work. Customers may have problems.

ek2_4.q: Today, car companies are developing self-driving cars. Do you think self-driving cars will become common in the future?
ek2_4.ja: 将来、自動運転車は広まると思いますか。

model.yes: Yes. → Self-driving cars can help elderly people who cannot drive. They may also reduce traffic accidents.
model.no: No. → Many people do not trust machines to drive safely. Also, many roads in Japan are narrow and busy.

ek2_4.q: In Japan, many stores are open 24 hours a day. Do you think stores should stay open all night?
ek2_4.ja: お店は夜通し営業するべきだと思いますか。

model.yes: Yes. → Some people work at night and need to buy things. Stores are also safe places for people who need help at night.
model.no: No. → It is hard for stores to find workers for the night. Closing at night can also save electricity.
